current.text: He is a rookie. He started the Warriors' preseason opener.
Golden State's projected starters are Curry, Podziemski, Lendeborg, Green and Horford. The more Draymond Green plays center, the more minutes open up for Lendeborg and Santos.
The Porzingis news gives him a usage boost, but not necessarily more minutes unless Green plays more center.
Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are out early in the season. Butler is out for at least half the season.
His numbers are expected to drop when Moody and Butler return, and Warriors players are expected to fade as the season goes on.
He is expected to be okay as a starter but to have rookie struggles.
Draft him as a round 10 to 11 flier. One expert would take him as high as pick 100 in category leagues and around 125 in points leagues.
He won Summer League MVP averaging 13 points. That line was boosted by 48% three-point shooting, which experts expect to regress.
Experts call the Warriors bad this season. The team is reportedly treating it as a gap year, worries about lottery odds and may rest veterans.
Steve Kerr rarely starts rookies, has little patience for them and often changes his announced starting lineup after a few games.
Golden State's depth is very poor. They struggle to field a 10-man rotation, so minutes should go up across the rotation.
Apart from Steph Curry, no one on the roster really creates his own shot or gets much usage.
The Warriors' schedule is good for fantasy playoffs that end March 28, but it includes 15 back-to-backs.

durable.text: He is an older rookie. He is 24 at the start of his first NBA season.
He fits in around others and is not a high-usage creator, so his usage will be low.
His fantasy appeal is a spread of rebounds, assists, steals and blocks. He is versatile and can grab a rebound and push the ball himself.
His shooting is inconsistent and his jumper is iffy.
Experts disagree on his free throws. One calls him a poor free throw shooter, and he shot under 70% FT in Summer League. A pre-draft note listed free throws as a college strength.
Threes are his weakest category for a forward. Projections differ a lot here: Yahoo has 1.3 threes per game and ESPN has 0.3.
Experts disagree on his defense. One calls him good defensively, and others expect defensive problems.
He has no clear position. He was a 20-usage player on a strong college team.

note: Yahoo ranks him 133 and ESPN ranks him 175. Both sites value him at about 1 USD, and he was not drafted in our league last season, so he is a 1 to 2 USD end-of-auction flier, worth it only for his spread of rebounds, assists, steals and blocks as a starter on a thin roster. He fits punt 3PM builds, but his projected 3PM swings from 0.3 (ESPN) to 1.3 (Yahoo) and his free throws are disputed. Early on, check whether Kerr keeps him in the starting lineup, his minutes and his FT%. Plan to move on or trade him before Butler and Moody return.
